topic: Geometric Representation on the Argand Plane
title: Where 3 + 2i Lives: Argand Plane Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Every real number has a home on the number line. So where does 3 + 2i live? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 4, Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations) Diya gives every complex number an address on a map, the way a Bengaluru address has a main and a cross: the Argand plane.

You will see the real axis and the imaginary axis drawn, then watch the points from the NCERT figure placed one by one (go x along, then y up). We see where real and purely imaginary numbers live, read the modulus as the distance from O and the conjugate as a mirror image in the real axis, then go one step beyond NCERT for JEE: the distance between two complex numbers, and how a rule like Re z = 2 draws a line while |z| = 2 draws a circle. A worked example, the exam trap about the centre of |z + 2i| = 3, two pause-and-think questions, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:

0:29 The Argand plane: real axis and imaginary axis
1:11 Live: plotting the NCERT points

2:01 Modulus and conjugate on the map
2:16 Distance between two complex numbers
2:46 Live: a rule draws a line or a circle
3:36 Worked example: distance from 1 + 2i to 4 - 2i
4:04 Exam trap: the centre of |z + 2i| = 3
4:21 Where it is asked
4:27 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:03 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 44): Polar Representation. What if every address were a distance and an angle, instead of along and up?
